post.summary: Close the seat baseline

201.description: The seat is taken from today by an assignment of source REQUEST, and a manual task is made that the acting IT Admin who pressed has already taken: it is in progress (IN_PROGRESS) under their account (claimedBy), recording the acting default responsible employee (appointed substitute or in-charge IT Admin) at creation time. Pressing again for the same request (for a request for a group, the same person), or another acting IT Admin pressing, makes nothing new: the answer is the task that exists, 201 with no warnings, still taken by whoever took it first. K5 takes no subscription and no seat. The seat is taken from the subscription of the plan, with no department filter: a subscription has no owning department. The task of a K1 grant carries k1Checklist (variant GRANT) to tick before it is completed. For the request of a service account the IT Admin enters the account identifier (not read from the request) and may name another active person of the owning department to answer for it (responsibleEmployeeId); the assignment is a service one, owned by that department and charged to its Unit Cost Center, with the purpose as its reason.

post.summary: Take a provisioning task to work on it

200.description: The task is completed under the name of this acting IT Admin for the task department. The evidence is a note of what was done, never a password or a key. A K4 grant names the free key of the store its seat is given (licenseKeyId; a key bought with the grant is imported into the store first): the key becomes ASSIGNED to the seat in the same transaction (LICENSE_KEY.ASSIGNED in the audit trail). A K2 or K4 grant taken from the pool with nothing bought records the cost it avoided; the request of a K4 grant taken from the pool gives back all of its commitment (GRANTED_FROM_POOL). A task of the kind EXTEND (the extension of a right whose renewal was approved) grants nothing: completing it writes the record that follows the renewed one and completes the renewal. The grant of a K1 seat is completed with k1Checklist: both steps of the card ticked (done true, each with the instant it was done, in the order of the card) and the evidence, written in k1Checklist.evidence or beside it; the steps are kept with the task and shown on its card. Another kind of grant, and an extension, take no k1Checklist.

200.description: The only end of a revocation that gives the seat back. K2 is completed as ACCOUNT_REMOVED with evidence, or as ALREADY_GONE with a note when the person removed the account themselves; K5 as OFF_SYSTEM_REVOKED with evidence; K4 as KEY_DEACTIVATED with evidence, and the IT Admin must say where its key goes (keyDisposition, required for K4): back to the store (RETURN_TO_STORE) or back and withdrawn from it at once (WITHDRAW, with a withdrawalReason: a key that may not move to another device), with LICENSE_KEY.RETURNED_TO_STORE (and LICENSE_KEY.WITHDRAWN) in the audit trail; K1 as RENEWAL_CANCELLED with the day the paid period ends (paidThroughOn), what is known of the access (UNTIL_PAID_END, or CUT with the day accessCutOn and its accessEvidence) and the checklist of the card (k1Checklist, required: the steps of the variant the card tells, DEPARTURE or STILL_EMPLOYED, each { code, done: true, doneAt } with doneAt not falling as the steps go (the same instant is in order; a step may be timed before the task was made), and the evidence in k1Checklist.evidence, or in evidence when the checklist has none; k1Checklist is refused for any other kind of grant). The assignment ends the same day for K2, K4 and K5, and for K1 at the end of the paid period or the day the access was cut, whichever is earlier; a K1 seat whose access runs on is reported as terminating. The completion writes no saving, invoice, contract or budget.

A row names the person, their department, the tool and the plan, the end day, the days past it and a debt flag set after seven days. Its status is WAITING_RENEWAL_DECISION while a renewal sent in time is not decided (the right stays as it is), READY_TO_REVOKE otherwise, and REVOCATION_OPEN once a revocation is under way, with that revocation. Filter by status, by debt or by department. A renewal that was approved ends the old record and the right leaves the queue.

A right that a renewal continues names the record that takes over. A grant that failed or was cancelled never held anything and is not listed. No price, cost, Cost Center, account identifier, license key or other person is answered: a K4 right shows that the software is granted, never its key. A start that is only the day of recording has a label and no grant date.

201.description: The usable IT Admin responsible for the subscription records, once per period and from its point of adjustment, what was done with the vendor: the choice (renew as it is, reduce, increase or cancel) with the seats the system counts for the next period (read them first; a number that is not that count is refused, and one above it is accepted only as the vendor minimum with the evidence in note), what the vendor did (as decided, refused, did otherwise; a result the vendor has not confirmed is recorded once it has) and the new period it confirmed, which starts on the renewal day and which a renewal, a reduction or an increase must carry (only a vendor that refused a plan by the month may leave it out) and so must a cancellation the vendor refused or did otherwise (it made a period anyway: an incident is raised for it). A cancellation is accepted only when no seat is needed, none is in effect and no request for the plan is open, and needs closure.dataExported and closure.adminsTransferred. The case is written complete in one transaction (state OUTCOME_RECORDED, deciderRole IT_ADMIN_IN_CHARGE): the new period continues the old one with the seats held on its first day, a seat ending on the renewal day stays on the old period. Writing after the renewal day is allowed (a late renewal). Finance is told. It opens no revocation, asks no head and creates no budget commitment. releasedAssignmentIds is no longer taken.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description: open: the requests that are not over, one that waits for the IT Admin to close the task of a withdrawal included. ended: the requests nothing is left to do in (completed, refused, failed, withdrawn, cancelled). Left out: both.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: One or more states of a request, comma-separated and none twice (for example PENDING,AWAITING_SPEND_DECISION); a draft is not a state of a request. Narrows within view when both are given.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The first moment the request was sent that is read (included). Must be earlier than to when both are given.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The moment after the last one the request was sent that is read (excluded).

parameters.name: departmentId
parameters.description: Only the requests sent from this department.

parameters.name: employeeId
parameters.description: Only the requests this person sent or is one of the people for.

parameters.name: flag
parameters.description: One or both of ONE_STEP (sent through the one-step route) and RESERVE_USED (the head confirmed the use of the reserve of the budget), comma-separated and none twice; a request has every flag named.

200.description: One page of the requests the role of the caller oversees, in every state, the newest sent first and then by id: pageSize 1 to 100, 20 when left out. An IT Admin reads every request sent in the organization; a spending approver the requests a spend step was opened on (one-step requests included), decided or not; Finance the requests whose spend was approved, so a commitment was made, released since or not. A caller with more than one of these roles reads all they reach. A draft is never listed. Narrowed by view (open or ended), by one or more states, by type, by the moment it was sent, by department, by a person who sent it or is one of the people for it, and by the flags ONE_STEP and RESERVE_USED. Each row names the plan or the proposed software, who sent it and who it is for, the department it was sent from, its state, its one-step or via-head routing, who it waits for at the need step, where a request that costs money stands on its way to the spending approver, the reason when it was refused, when it was withdrawn, and whether the head confirmed the use of the reserve. No price, amount, figure of a budget, result of a check, commitment or reason Finance wrote is answered; the detail, the time, the people and the history of a request are read by its id.

Narrowed by view (open or ended), by one or more states, by type, by the moment it was sent and by a person who sent it or is one of the people for it. awaitingMe says that it waits for the head now. Each row names the plan or the proposed software, who sent it and who it is for, the department it was sent from, its state, its one-step or via-head routing, who it waits for at the need step, where a request that costs money stands on its way to the spending approver, the reason when it was refused, when it was withdrawn, and whether the head confirmed the use of the reserve. No price, amount, figure of a budget, result of a check, commitment or reason Finance wrote is answered; the detail, the time, the people and the history of a request are read by its id.

200.description: The report of the revocations of the departures and the transfers whose window of revocations opens from `from` to `to` (the day after the last working day, or the day after the end of the grace). The deadline of a window is its first working day: the IT Admin is on time when the last task of the departure or the transfer is completed by then. The figures are the departures or transfers completed, on time, open and overdue today, the median of the working days the completed ones took and the share on time; each row is one IT Admin or one department, those with the most overdue first. A departure is overdue as the list of departures says it (`revocationOverdue=true`), a right with no task opened included; a transfer, by a task still to do (its tasks carry no due date of their own). `transferReRequests` counts the requests sent again by a person in the grace of their transfer for software they already hold and those granted by the last day of the grace. It is an operational figure beside the overviews, not a KPI. The Super Admin reads the whole company, an IT Admin only the departments they are in charge of or stand in for.

k1Checklist.description: Present on a K1 task that can still be completed (the steps to tick) and on one completed with a checklist (what was ticked and when). The variant is decided by the server. GRANT is the grant of a K1 seat: register on the company email of the person themself, and do not turn on multi-factor sign-in with a personal device. For a K1 revocation it comes from why the seat is revoked: DEPARTURE (a person who leaves: reset the mailbox password, Forgot password on the software, sign out every session, turn off the renewal, record the evidence and, only on the last K1 revocation of the person, lock the mailbox: while another K1 revocation of the same person is not over this task has the five steps before the lock) or STILL_EMPLOYED (turn off the renewal, record the evidence). The system does not control Google or Microsoft 365: the IT Admin does the steps there and ticks them here, in order. Null on any other task (an extension, another kind of seat), on a K1 task completed before the checklist, and on one cancelled or closed as failed.

suggestRenewal.description: The term ends within the year, or ends before it and still runs today: a Renew line is suggested.

versionsAdjustment.description: Of versionsTotal, what the adjustments approved in the year gave to (positive) or took from (negative) the base of the approved versions; the versions in the rows are as they were approved.

unallocated.description: `available` less versionsTotal, never below nothing: what is not allocated, which a supplement or a reduction of the annual ceiling may take.

versionsOutsideListed.description: Of versionsTotal, what belongs to a Cost Center whose department is not listed (a department that stopped).

versionsInOtherCurrency.description: Counted versions left out of the sums because they are not in the currency of the cycle.

overBy.description: What the versions are over `available` by; zero when they are not.

baselineAllowed.description: Finance may build the first version of the department from the baseline now: the same check as the version of source BASELINE.

poolLines.description: The line of the shared pool of each subscription with an invoice or a seat-month in the month (Finance only; empty for a manager).

priceIncrease.description: The price increase already known: the rise of the price of a seat over what the commitment was made at, for the seats and months left; a price that fell adds nothing.

forecast.description: The forecast of the end of the year: spent + spent after the month + (held + waiting) x (1 + k) + price increase already known.

paceBasisPoints.description: The spent through the end of the month over the base of the months gone, in hundredths of a percent (11.200 is 112 %), rounded up; null when the Cost Center has no base.

light.description: The light of the Cost Center at the close: RED when the forecast is above the base and the reserve; YELLOW when it is above the base or the pace is above 110 % of the schedule; UNDER from June when the forecast is under 70 % of the base; GREEN otherwise. revocation.description: What the case asks of the IT Admin by way of revocation, worked out when it is read from the Request the person sent for the same software (an account on a company asset waits at most ten working days for it to reach the step of the spending approver).

amount.description: What was spent, in dong. Only for RECORD_SPENT, and then above nothing.

required.description: The IT Admin has an account to revoke for this case: it is open and on a company asset, and the person has no Request that was approved. False for a personal account, a closed case, or a person whose Request was approved (the grant then goes by the task of that Request).

due.description: The IT Admin has the revocation to do now: nothing to wait for, the ceiling has passed with the Request not yet at the step of the spending approver, or the Request came to that step after the ceiling. Worked out when the case is read, never stored.

revocation.description: What the case asks of the IT Admin by way of revocation, worked out when it is read from the Request the person sent for the same software (an account on a company asset waits at most ten working days for it to reach the step of the spending approver).

target.description: The read route to open; null means open the list of notifications.

status.description: PENDING for a call just started. The same revision asked again gives the call already kept for it, in the state it is in. sourceStale.description: True when the queue of the person changed since the summary was composed.

simulated.description: True khi bản tóm tắt do chế độ giả lập dựng, không phải model AI; FE luôn hiển thị nhãn 'Giả lập — không phải AI'.

lines.description: The checked lines whose step still waits for the person, in the order of the queue; at most 20.

errorCode.description: Why a call shows nothing, when it does not: AI.PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE, AI.PROVIDER_TIMEOUT, AI.OUTPUT_INVALID, AI.NO_VALID_OUTPUT, AI.SOURCE_UNREADABLE or AI.INTERNAL_ERROR. A state of the call read here, never an HTTP error.

providerMode.description: Where the answer came from: MODEL, the AI service; SIMULATED, the simulation that calls no model (show the label 'Giả lập — không phải AI').

context.description: The allow-listed context sent to the AI service, with opaque references (R001, C001) in place of ids. A JSON object.

promptText.description: The prompt that was sent to the model; null while the call has not been answered.

rawResponse.description: What the model answered, as it came; null while the call has not been answered.

parsed.description: The output of the AI service as it parsed it, a JSON object; null when it did not answer or could not parse it.

hasDraft.description: Whether a draft is open; only the Super Admin is told, everyone else reads null.
